Method of Attack: Use of droppers (dual or multiple-stage infection process) to bypass Google Play Store security scans
Droppers request minimal permissions and delay malicious payload execution to evade detection
Droppers download and install more potent mobile banking trojans after gaining permissions
Malicious code activation triggered by commands from command-and-control (C&C) servers or user device intensive use
Attack Vector: Malicious apps uploaded to Google Play Store using droppers
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious downloader apps disguised as legitimate applications on Google Play Store
Command-and-control (C&C) servers fetching over 1,000 malware samples
Similar dropper app code reused across campaigns (e.g., Exobot dropper panel)
Delayed execution and activation of malicious payloads triggered by C&C commands or user behavior
